answer: A refundable stake escrow makes fake identities expensive: every agent must lock a deposit before it can trade, and the deposit is slashed if the agent is caught running duplicate identities. Like tending an orchard, each tree needs its own plot of land — you cannot plant a thousand junipers on one jetty and claim each is a separate farm. An attacker must fund every fake identity separately, so the cost of a Sybil swarm scales with its size while honest agents pay once and get their stake back.
